The edge: one draft plan, served live, with its notes beside it loden

Loden (the edge: one draft plan, served live) put the draft at the repository's root, so anyone opening the repository sees whether a plan is being drafted. Since then two things moved. First, nankeen (landed plans aren't edited from the TUI) declined editing, and Jeff named what he wants instead: "a way to indicate [past plans] need revisited. Maybe with some notes." Those notes need a home, and it isn't plans/. Second, Jeff said where that home is: "this is just one developer's idea here about something", and its value would be "look at my branch, here's what I'm thinking about this old plan." The revisit is how main deals with it.

Asked in loden's frame: is the root still the right place for work in progress? What moved is our understanding. Loden had one kind of work in progress, the draft. Now there are two, and both are a person's thinking, not testimony. So plans/ holds testimony and nothing else, and everything still being thought about shares one folder.

This is the first plan that crosses the old line between phoropter and the TUI. It changes the format, the dev server and the TUI in the same work.

Decision: The draft, its notes, and requests on landed plans live in drafts/

where src/draft.ts file page

quote export const DRAFT = 'plan.draft.md';

Because (Jeff): "maybe we move to a '/plans-drafts/' directory, and the current plan is in there, and any of these notes for old plans." The one draft is drafts/plan.draft.md, and its notes are drafts/plan.draft.notes.md. Loden's rules hold: one draft, one fixed name, nothing to configure. A top-level folder keeps what loden wanted from the root: anyone opening the repository sees whether something is in progress. It's called drafts/ (Jeff). It's short, it says "not yet", and the guide already calls a draft a draft. The requests in it are drafts of a different kind: a person's case for a revisit, before anyone has written one. plans.wip/ and plans-drafts/ were weighed. The name may become a seam for configuration someday, for a repository that already has a drafts/ (Jeff), but not now.

Decision: A request to revisit is a notes file on a landed plan, kept in drafts/

where plans/2026-10-31-nankeen.md › Editing a landed plan from the TUI

entry Decline: Editing a landed plan from the TUI in nankeen

Because (Jeff, then Claude): nankeen declined editing a landed plan. A note on one is the conversation Jeff wanted instead of an edit. For plans/2026-10-31-ramie.md, the request is drafts/2026-10-31-ramie.notes.md, in the annotating agreement's shape. Its annotates: line names plans/2026-10-31-ramie.md, so it stands alone. A note quotes an entry's heading, or has no quote and is about the whole plan.

The agreement puts notes beside their file, and these are in another folder. That's a deliberate variation, with this reason: plans/ holds testimony only. The guide says so where it restates the agreement. A landed plan never changes, so its notes can't come loose from what they quote, and they need no hash check.

Decision: A revisit answers a request, and converting it deletes the request

where plans/2026-10-31-loden.md › Converting a draft writes the plan and removes the draft

entry Decision: Converting a draft writes the plan and removes the draft in loden

Because (Claude, not asked): loden's conversion deletes the draft's notes, since what mattered from them is in the plan's reasons by then. A request works the same way. The agent drafts a revisit (revisits: the plan), and its intro cites the request. When the revisit converts, the request it answers is deleted with the draft's own notes. If the agent thinks the plan still holds, it says so in a note of its own in the request file. The request stays until the person agrees, or a revisit lands anyway. The person can always overrule the agent.

Decision: Requests travel on branches, and main changes only by revisit

where plans/2026-10-31-loden.md › Ignoring the draft in git is a suggestion, not a requirement

entry Decision: Ignoring the draft in git is a suggestion, not a requirement in loden

Because (Jeff): "the supersedes thing is how we deal with it in main. I can even see an ongoing branch called 'plans' where the lead developers do a lot of this." Loden made ignoring the draft a suggestion, and that holds for all of drafts/. On a branch, committing drafts/ is how a teammate or a mentor reads a request or a draft before anything is decided. On main, what lands is plans. The guide describes a long-lived "plans" branch as one way a team can work, not a rule. Phoropter doesn't care which branch it's on. In this repository, where Jeff and Claude work on main, drafts/ is ignored (Jeff). Here the pair is the team, a request is seen on the dev server and in the TUI, and nothing in drafts/ should land on main by accident.

Decision: The dev server shows a plan's requests on the plan's page

where src/serve.ts file page

quote function withDraftLink(html: string, here: string): string {

Because (Claude, not asked): loden's ground holds: a built site is a function of one commit and never shows drafts/, even when it's committed. The dev server shows work in progress, so it adds a plan's requests to that plan's page as it serves it: the same annotation items a draft has, after the entries they quote, and whole-plan notes first. The home list marks a plan that has a request. The profile defines both.

Decision: The guide and both CLAUDE.md files say where work in progress lives

where guide.md file page

quote A repository has at most one draft, `plan.draft.md` at its root.

Because (Claude, not asked): the guide is the format, so it changes in the same work. It gets the folder, requests and how a revisit answers them, and the notes-elsewhere variation. The root CLAUDE.md tells the agent to look in drafts/ for requests at the start of a session and raise any it finds before other work. Otherwise a request is a note in a drawer. The TUI's CLAUDE.md changes its draft paths.

Decision: In the TUI, a on a landed plan writes a request

where tui/internal/tui/screens.go file page

quote m.status = "only a draft takes notes; a plan is testimony"

Because (Jeff): this is the feature nankeen pointed at. On a landed plan's entry, a writes a note quoting its heading into the plan's request file. On its About row, a writes a note on the whole plan. The plan's page names its file, so the TUI knows which request file to write. The message on screen becomes "a plan takes notes, never edits". The TUI reads requests back from the dev server's plan page, the same page the agent reads, never from the file.

Decision: The TUI finds the draft where the page says it is

where tui/internal/notes/notes.go file page

quote func DraftOnDisk(dir string) bool {

Because (Claude, measured): answering already opens the draft by the page header's file, so it follows the move with no change. Checking for a draft the site doesn't serve looks in drafts/. The TUI's sample draft is copied to drafts/plan.draft.md.

Decline: Reading a draft from the root as well, for a while

Because (Claude, not asked): loden's reason for one fixed name was "nothing to remember to pass." Two places to look is a second name to remember. No repository has a draft at the root today, so nothing is stranded.

Decline: A "needs revisit" flag without a note

Because (Claude, not asked): a flag with no reason is a backlog item. The note is the flag, and it says what moved, which is the first thing a revisit needs.

Guess: A request to revisit gets a draft back without being asked twice
